title: Paul's unusual opening word prepares his appeal
english: In many of his letters Paul places an unusual word at the start, one that is preparatory for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he shows the credibility of his appeal through his own worth—and his worth is being in chains.
translator_notes: The text is a fragment (in catenis).
The fragment begins with a title/heading indicating it is a fragment of a commentary on Philemon.
baehrens: PG 65; Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (Khazarzar) u01 open
orientation: Severianus is explaining how Paul opens the letter to Philemon with a striking word that sets up the request he is about to make for Onesimus.
